A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
aCGH is an effective tool to identify genomic abnormalities, but it should not be used as a stand-alone technique for diagnostic purposes.
the aCGH can provide a better genomic diagnosis for patients with clonal cytogenomic abnormalities, but it cannot be used as a substitute for a karyotypic analysis.
the aCGH can detect most of the clinically significant genomic changes in elderly patients with myeloproliferative neoplasms.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the aCGH is a powerful tool to detect cryptic abnormalities that are undetectable by routine cytogenetic analysis.
genomic diagnosis will be a better approach to delineate genomic content of chromosomal and subchromosomal abnormalities in patients with hematopoietic neoplasm.
aCGH is a powerful tool to detect genomic abnormalities and to characterize genomic breakpoints.
